runner.note: No suite runner executes this directory. The six block cases are declarative: block-independence-vectors.json states inputs, rows and visibility under D-585 and nothing evaluates them, so they are not evidence that any block is enforced. The six merge cases are different in one respect and the difference is worth stating exactly: scripts/repository/validate_social_surface_contracts.py folds each case's device set under the file's own merge_rule, in both orderings, and compares the result to expected_availability. That executes the rule against the fixture. It does not execute a server, a lease or a pulse, and no presence surface exists to execute.

cases.title: Enumerate the ten social and ranking scenarios the suite owes
cases.note: This case asserts that the scenario list parses and covers the named ten. It asserts nothing about ranking, blocks, boards or presence, and it must never be cited as social conformance. The suite has no negative case because it has no executable case at all.

cases.title: block does not remove friendship
cases.note: The friendship row survives unchanged. Visibility is denied in both directions because a one-way hole is itself a disclosure: the blocked party would see a gap where a person used to be.

cases.title: unblock restores visibility
cases.note: Nothing was destroyed, so nothing has to be restored. Under the previous contract the friendship reached a terminal blocked state and this case was unreachable.

cases.title: friendship removal does not clear a block
cases.note: The independence holds in the other direction too. Ending a friendship is not an implicit unblock.

cases.title: block is directional in the row
cases.note: Two independent rows, because the relation is directional in storage even though its visibility effect is symmetric. b blocking a is not a no-op just because a already blocked b: if a later unblocks, b's block still stands.

cases.title: one sided unblock leaves the other block standing
cases.note: The surviving block still denies both directions. This is the case a symmetric boolean would get wrong.

cases.title: rivalry is not a block state
cases.note: rival_edges.state no longer admits blocked. The edge stays active and is suppressed at read time, so an unblock does not need to guess which rivalries to revive.

cases.title: one active device and one expired device merge to online
cases.note: The case the fold exists for. A last-write merge reading the desktop lease second answers offline and the participant disappears while still working.

cases.title: an idle device and an expired device merge to idle
cases.note: Idle outranks expired. An expired lease is an absence of evidence about one device, not evidence the account is gone.

cases.title: a revoked device does not raise the account answer
cases.note: Negative. A revoked device contributing presence would let a device the participant removed keep reporting them present, which is a security act being undone by a projection. The case is negative and expects accept, which is not a contradiction: nothing here refuses a request, so there is no reason code to name. What it proves is that the fold does not manufacture presence, and a fold that answered online for any of these three would be wrong in the direction that matters.

cases.title: three devices in three states merge to the most present
cases.note: The fold is over a set and not a pair, which is where an implementation written for two devices stops agreeing.

cases.title: every device expired merges to offline
cases.note: Negative. No ordering of expired leases may produce a present account. The case is negative and expects accept, which is not a contradiction: nothing here refuses a request, so there is no reason code to name. What it proves is that the fold does not manufacture presence, and a fold that answered online for any of these three would be wrong in the direction that matters.

cases.title: an account with no lease row merges to offline
cases.note: Negative. An empty device set must not fall through to a default that means present. The case is negative and expects accept, which is not a contradiction: nothing here refuses a request, so there is no reason code to name. What it proves is that the fold does not manufacture presence, and a fold that answered online for any of these three would be wrong in the direction that matters.
